page.layout: One column of text; marginal notes in the right margin; catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: 6. Vt autem ęger animus semper errat: ita hi, cum suum quisque idolum implo-ret, bis peccant, cum & sibi pro arbitrio suo numina fingant, & si maximè unum Deum adorét, μονόφθαλμον esse uelint, qui ad ipsorum peccata uel cæcus sit, uel con-niueat, & laborantibus euestigiò succur-rens, molestia eos liberet. Quàntò re-ctius Ethnicus ille Xenophō statuit, Deū in secundis studiosè colendum, ut in ad-uersis dexter & propitius nobis adsit.

7. Deinde confugiut ad alia salutis suæ præsidia, quæ à secundis causis subministrari uidentur. Vt cum nautæ, salute pro-pè desperata, ἀπολλύντι γε θυμῷ[?] iacturam faciunt. Ac si tale quid ex sententia succedat, & optato fine potiantur, ne sui domestici idoli (quod φίλαυτοι homines unicè colunt) obliti, suiq; dissimiles uideantur, numini aliquam, industriq; & labori suo optimam salutis suæ partem, non sine sacri-legio, adscribunt.

8. Qui uerò in utramuis indormiunt Lectio 15.[?] aurem, ne ultima Octobris, 1578[?] sensus malorum publicorum, cōscientiam torqueat, multis modis peccant & errant. Peccant, cum nec Deo glo-riam dant, nec sibi cōsulunt, nec aliis com

page.notes: Marginal notes: "Lectio 15." and "ultima Octobris, 1578" read from a worn right margin; the last letters of "Octobris" and the figures "1578" are doubtful (the scan shows "Oft" and "1ʃ8"). The Greek "ἀπολλύντι γε θυμῷ" is read from a small, blurred line and is uncertain. "ęger" is copied with the printed ę. The line "nec aliis com" ends without a printed hyphen; the catchword "patiun-" carries the hyphen as printed. The "e" at the foot is taken as the signature, though it sits near the centre. The page is set in roman type; no black letter. Nothing is illegible.
